title: MPSC Order — Case No. U-20591: Grants the motion

PRESENT: Hon. Daniel C. Scripps, Chair 

Hon. Tremaine L. Phillips, Commissioner 

Hon. Katherine L. Peretick, Commissioner 

ORDER 

On September 24, 2021, Indiana Michigan Power Company (I&M) filed a motion in Case 
No. U-20591 requesting approval to extend its December 15, 2021 integrated resource plan 
(IRP) filing to February 28, 2022 (motion to extend deadline). I&M explains that the company 
serves retail customers in both Indiana and Michigan and that its electric system is completely 
integrated and operates as a single utility. I&M’s motion, pp. 1-2. I&M further explains that it 
has submitted a total company IRP with the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission since 1995 

Page 2 
U-20591 et al. 

and that recent developments have significantly impacted the company’s IRP modeling 
assumptions that will delay its filing in Indiana. Id., p. 2. 

In further support of its motion: 
I&M is proposing a new Michigan IRP filing date that provides several benefits: 
i) it allows the necessary time to run modeling scenarios which take into account 
the impact of the Rockport settlement on I&M’s total company IRP, ii) it 
coordinates the filling date to account for the workload and other case activity of 
other stakeholders, including [Commission] Staff, iii) provides ample time for 
stakeholder input and engagement in the remainder of I&M’s IRP stakeholder 
process and iv) provides I&M and its third party contractor a reasonable amount 
of time to take steps to assure the quality of the IRP modeling and preparation and 
filing of the IRP in Michigan. 

Id., p. 3. 

On September 27, 2021, the Commission’s Executive Secretary issued a Notice of 
Opportunity to Respond to I&M’s motion to extend deadline. On October 11, 2021, Great Lakes 
Renewable Energy Association filed a response noting no objection to the motion. No other 
responses were filed. 

The Commission has reviewed I&M’s motion to extend deadline and finds that the motion 
should be granted. The Commission finds that I&M’s stated benefits of extending the IRP filing 
provide sufficient cause for extending the filing to February 28, 2022. Additionally, the 
Commission finds that the filing of the company’s biennial Public Utility Regulatory Policies 
Act of 1978 avoided cost review, as provided in the March 19, 2021 order in Case Nos. U-18092 
et al., is also included in the February 28, 2022 IRP filing extension. 

Page 3 
U-20591 et al. 

THEREFORE, IT IS ORDERED that the motion filed by Indiana Michigan Power Company 
to extend the deadline for filing its integrated resource plan is granted. Indiana Michigan Power 
Company shall file its integrated resource plan on or before February 28, 2022, and shall also 
include its Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 avoided cost review in its integrated 
resource plan filing. 

The Commission reserves jurisdiction and may issue further orders as necessary. 

Page 4 
U-20591 et al. 

Any party desiring to appeal this order must do so in the appropriate court within 30 days 
after issuance and notice of this order, pursuant to MCL 462.26. To comply with the Michigan 
Rules of Court’s requirement to notify the Commission of an appeal, appellants shall send 
required notices to both the Commission’s Executive Secretary and to the Commission’s Legal 
Counsel. Electronic notifications should be sent to the Executive Secretary at 
mpscedockets@michigan.gov and to the Michigan Department of the Attorney General – Public 
Service Division at pungp1@michigan.gov. In lieu of electronic submissions, paper copies of 
such notifications may be sent to the Executive Secretary and the Attorney General – Public 
Service Division at 7109 W. Saginaw Hwy., Lansing, MI 48917.
